content.title: About
content.content: The hamburger slider is a miniature version of the classic burger, usually weighing 30–50 g, served in multiple pieces per portion. It consists of a small bun, a beef patty, cheese, pickles, onion and sauce. It is commonly offered in fast‑food outlets as a quick snack or as part of a combo.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Sliders first appeared in the United States in the early 1980s as part of bar and fast‑food menus.
The name “slider” comes from the idea that the bite “slides” easily into the mouth, emphasizing speed and convenience.
In many countries sliders are served in sets of three or four, allowing diners to sample several flavors in one order.
Patty batches are often pre‑cooked and reheated on a grill or in a microwave to speed up service.
Sliders are a popular item in “speed‑eating” contests, where participants may consume up to 10 pieces in a minute.

items.title: Protein source
items.content: The beef patty provides high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Red meat is rich in heme iron, which is more readily absorbed than plant‑based iron.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Hamburger sliders supply vitamin B12, niacin and riboflavin, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Portion control
items.content: The small size makes it easier to manage calorie intake compared with a full‑size burger.

items.title: Zinc content
items.content: Beef provides zinc, an important mineral for immune function.

items.title: High saturated fat
items.content: The patty and cheese can contain significant amounts of saturated fat, which may raise cardiovascular risk when consumed frequently.

items.title: Salt and sauces
items.content: Sauces and pickles often add a lot of sodium, potentially contributing to high blood pressure.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: The bun is typically made from wheat flour, making the product unsuitable for people with celiac disease.

items.title: Calorie density
items.content: Even though each piece is small, eating several sliders can quickly exceed daily calorie recommendations.

items.title: Bacterial contamination
items.content: Undercooked beef may harbor pathogens such as E. coli or salmonella.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Sliders are usually eaten by hand, holding the bottom bun. They pair well with fries, barbecue sauce, or fresh vegetables. For a lighter option, add lettuce, tomato, or swap the beef patty for chicken or a plant‑based alternative.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store prepared sliders in the refrigerator at 0–4 °C for up to 2 days. Frozen sliders keep well for up to 3 months; thaw completely and reheat to an internal temperature of 75 °C before serving.
